current: Bending an indium bar makes a high-pitched 'cry' as its crystals slip.
corrected: "Bending an indium bar makes a high-pitched 'cry' as its crystals suddenly twin."
source: Wikipedia Indium (crackling sound 'due to crystal twinning'); same explanation as for tin cry
reason: The cry comes from deformation twinning, where parts of a crystal suddenly flip into a mirror-image orientation. It does not come from slip (dislocation glide), which is a different and quiet deformation mechanism. A fact that has to be strictly true should not name the wrong mechanism.

current: Named columbium; confused with tantalum until Heinrich Rose separated them in 1844.
corrected: "Named columbium; confused with tantalum until Heinrich Rose showed in 1844 that it was a different element."
source: Wikipedia Niobium, History section; RSC periodic table (niobium)
reason: Rose did not separate niobium from tantalum. He showed that tantalite held a second element, which he called niobium. He also wrongly claimed a third element, pelopium. Blomstrand showed the difference unequivocally in 1864, and Marignac worked out the actual separation, by fractional crystallization, in 1864-1866. Sources give 1844 or 1846 for Rose's work, so the year can stay.
